original.title: Toward a Theory of Stakeholder Identification and Salience: Defining the Principle of who and What Really Counts

core_idea: Managers pay attention to stakeholders according to three attributes: power (ability to impose their will), legitimacy (appropriateness of their claim) and urgency (time-sensitivity and criticality of the claim). The more attributes a stakeholder has, the more salient it is to managers.
key_concepts_note: Use the concepts already stored for this theory in the library (theories.concepts).
when_to_use: Which stakeholders do managers actually prioritize, and why?
How does a stakeholder gain or lose salience over time?
Typical data: interviews with managers, document analysis, surveys, case studies.
common_mistakes: Classifying stakeholders once, as if salience never changes.
Assuming managers' perceptions equal objective attributes.
Confusing salience (attention) with importance or moral standing.
